L16: ## 29.38 Relatively ample sheaves
L17: 
L18: Let $X$ be a scheme and $\mathcal{L}$ an invertible sheaf on $X$. Then $\mathcal{L}$ is ample on $X$ if $X$ is quasi-compact and every point of $X$ is contained in an affine open of the form $X_ s$, where $s \in \Gamma (X, \mathcal{L}^{\otimes n})$ and $n \geq 1$, see Properties, Definition 【11†28.27.1】. We turn this into a relative notion as follows.
L19: 
L20: reference
L21: 【12†Definition 29.38.1.】 Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_ X$-module. We say $\mathcal{L}$ is relatively ample, or $f$-relatively ample, or ample on $X/S$, or $f$-ample if $f : X \to S$ is quasi-compact, and if for every affine open $V \subset S$ the restriction of $\mathcal{L}$ to the open subscheme $f^{-1}(V)$ of $X$ is ample.
L22: We note that the existence of a relatively ample sheaf on $X$ does not force the morphism $X \to S$ to be of finite type.
L23: 
L24: 【13†Lemma 29.38.2.】 Let $X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_ X$-module. Let $n \geq 1$. Then $\mathcal{L}$ is $f$-ample if and only if $\mathcal{L}^{\otimes n}$ is $f$-ample.
L25: 
L26: Proof. This follows from Properties, Lemma 【14†28.27.2】. $\square$
L27: 【15†Lemma 29.38.3.】 Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. If there exists an $f$-ample invertible sheaf, then $f$ is separated.
L28: 
L29: Proof. Being separated is local on the base (see Schemes, Lemma 【16†26.21.7】 for example; it also follows easily from the definition). Hence we may assume $S$ is affine and $X$ has an ample invertible sheaf. In this case the result follows from Properties, Lemma 【17†28.27.8】. $\square$
L30: There are many ways to characterize relatively ample invertible sheaves, analogous to the equivalent conditions in Properties, Proposition 【18†28.27.13】. We will add these here as needed.
L31: 
L32: reference
L33: 
L34: 【19†Lemma 29.38.4.】 Let $f : X \to S$ be a quasi-compact morphism of schemes. Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible sheaf on $X$. The following are equivalent:
L35: 
L36:   1. The invertible sheaf $\mathcal{L}$ is $f$-ample.
L37:   2. There exists an open covering $S = \bigcup V_ i$ such that each $\mathcal{L}|_{f^{-1}(V_ i)}$ is ample relative to $f^{-1}(V_ i) \to V_ i$.
L38: 
L39:   3. There exists an affine open covering $S = \bigcup V_ i$ such that each $\mathcal{L}|_{f^{-1}(V_ i)}$ is ample.
L40: 
L41:   4. There exists a quasi-coherent graded $\mathcal{O}_ S$-algebra $\mathcal{A}$ and a map of graded $\mathcal{O}_ X$-algebras $\psi : f^*\mathcal{A} \to \bigoplus _{d \geq 0} \mathcal{L}^{\otimes d}$ such that $U(\psi ) = X$ and
L42: \[ r_{\mathcal{L}, \psi } : X \longrightarrow \underline{\text{Proj}}_ S(\mathcal{A}) \]
L43: 
L44: is an open immersion (see Constructions, Lemma 【20†27.19.1】 for notation).
L45: 
L46:   5. The morphism $f$ is quasi-separated and part (4) above holds with $\mathcal{A} = f_*(\bigoplus _{d \geq 0} \mathcal{L}^{\otimes d})$ and $\psi $ the adjunction mapping.
L47: 
L48:   6. Same as (4) but just requiring $r_{\mathcal{L}, \psi }$ to be an immersion.
L49: Proof. It is immediate from the definition that (1) implies (2) and (2) implies (3). It is clear that (5) implies (4).
L50: Assume (3) holds for the affine open covering $S = \bigcup V_ i$. We are going to show (5) holds. Since each $f^{-1}(V_ i)$ has an ample invertible sheaf we see that $f^{-1}(V_ i)$ is separated (Properties, Lemma 【17†28.27.8】). Hence $f$ is separated. By Schemes, Lemma 【21†26.24.1】 we see that $\mathcal{A} = f_*(\bigoplus _{d \geq 0} \mathcal{L}^{\otimes d})$ is a quasi-coherent graded $\mathcal{O}_ S$-algebra.
L51: Denote $\psi : f^*\mathcal{A} \to \bigoplus _{d \geq 0} \mathcal{L}^{\otimes d}$ the adjunction mapping. The description of the open $U(\psi )$ in Constructions, Section 【22†27.19】 and the definition of ampleness of $\mathcal{L}|_{f^{-1}(V_ i)}$ show that $U(\psi ) = X$.
L52: Moreover, Constructions, Lemma 【20†27.19.1】 part (3) shows that the restriction of $r_{\mathcal{L}, \psi }$ to $f^{-1}(V_ i)$ is the same as the morphism from Properties, Lemma 【23†28.27.9】 which is an open immersion according to Properties, Lemma 【24†28.27.11】. Hence (5) holds.
L53: Let us show that (4) implies (1). Assume (4). Denote $\pi : \underline{\text{Proj}}_ S(\mathcal{A}) \to S$ the structure morphism. Choose $V \subset S$ affine open. By Constructions, Definition 【25†27.16.7】 we see that $\pi ^{-1}(V) \subset \underline{\text{Proj}}_ S(\mathcal{A})$ is equal to $\text{Proj}(A)$ where $A = \mathcal{A}(V)$ as a graded ring. Hence $r_{\mathcal{L}, \psi }$ maps $f^{-1}(V)$ isomorphically onto a quasi-compact open of $\text{Proj}(A)$.
L54: Moreover, $\mathcal{L}^{\otimes d}$ is isomorphic to the pullback of $\mathcal{O}_{\text{Proj}(A)}(d)$ for some $d \geq 1$. (See part (3) of Constructions, Lemma 【20†27.19.1】 and the final statement of Constructions, Lemma 【26†27.14.1】.) This implies that $\mathcal{L}|_{f^{-1}(V)}$ is ample by Properties, Lemmas 【27†28.27.12】 and 【14†28.27.2】.
L55: Assume (6). By the equivalence of (1) - (5) above we see that the property of being relatively ample on $X/S$ is local on $S$. Hence we may assume that $S$ is affine, and we have to show that $\mathcal{L}$ is ample on $X$. In this case the morphism $r_{\mathcal{L}, \psi }$ is identified with the morphism, also denoted $r_{\mathcal{L}, \psi } : X \to \text{Proj}(A)$ associated to the map $\psi : A = \mathcal{A}(V) \to \Gamma _*(X, \mathcal{L})$.
L56: (See references above.) As above we also see that $\mathcal{L}^{\otimes d}$ is the pullback of the sheaf $\mathcal{O}_{\text{Proj}(A)}(d)$ for some $d \geq 1$. Moreover, since $X$ is quasi-compact we see that $X$ gets identified with a closed subscheme of a quasi-compact open subscheme $Y \subset \text{Proj}(A)$. By Constructions, Lemma 【28†27.10.6】 (see also Properties, Lemma 【27†28.27.12】) we see that $\mathcal{O}_ Y(d')$ is an ample invertible sheaf on $Y$ for some $d' \geq 1$.
L57: Since the restriction of an ample sheaf to a closed subscheme is ample, see Properties, Lemma 【29†28.27.3】 we conclude that the pullback of $\mathcal{O}_ Y(d')$ is ample. Combining these results with Properties, Lemma 【14†28.27.2】 we conclude that $\mathcal{L}$ is ample as desired. $\square$
L58: reference

L60: 【30†Lemma 29.38.5.】 Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_ X$-module. Assume $S$ affine. Then $\mathcal{L}$ is $f$-relatively ample if and only if $\mathcal{L}$ is ample on $X$.
L61: 
L62: Proof. Immediate from Lemma 【19†29.38.4】 and the definitions. $\square$
L63: 
L64: reference
L65: 
L66: 【31†Lemma 29.38.6.】 Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Then $f$ is quasi-affine if and only if $\mathcal{O}_ X$ is $f$-relatively ample.
L67: Proof. Follows from Properties, Lemma 【32†28.28.1】 and the definitions. $\square$
L68: 
L69: 【33†Lemma 29.38.7.】 Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes, $\mathcal{M}$ an invertible $\mathcal{O}_ Y$-module, and $\mathcal{L}$ an invertible $\mathcal{O}_ X$-module.
L70: 
L71:   1. If $\mathcal{L}$ is $f$-ample and $\mathcal{M}$ is ample, then $\mathcal{L} \otimes f^*\mathcal{M}^{\otimes a}$ is ample for $a \gg 0$.
L72: 
L73:   2. If $\mathcal{M}$ is ample and $f$ quasi-affine, then $f^*\mathcal{M}$ is ample.
L74: Proof. Assume $\mathcal{L}$ is $f$-ample and $\mathcal{M}$ ample. By assumption $Y$ and $f$ are quasi-compact (see Definition 【12†29.38.1】 and Properties, Definition 【11†28.27.1】). Hence $X$ is quasi-compact. By Properties, Lemma 【17†28.27.8】 the scheme $Y$ is separated and by Lemma 【15†29.38.3】 the morphism $f$ is separated. Hence $X$ is separated by Schemes, Lemma 【34†26.21.12】. Pick $x \in X$.
L75: We can choose $m \geq 1$ and $t \in \Gamma (Y, \mathcal{M}^{\otimes m})$ such that $Y_ t$ is affine and $f(x) \in Y_ t$. Since $\mathcal{L}$ restricts to an ample invertible sheaf on $f^{-1}(Y_ t) = X_{f^*t}$ we can choose $n \geq 1$ and $s \in \Gamma (X_{f^*t}, \mathcal{L}^{\otimes n})$ with $x \in (X_{f^*t})_ s$ with $(X_{f^*t})_ s$ affine.
L76: By Properties, Lemma 【35†28.18.2】 part (2) whose assumptions are satisfied by the above, there exists an integer $e \geq 1$ and a section $s' \in \Gamma (X, \mathcal{L}^{\otimes n} \otimes f^*\mathcal{M}^{\otimes em})$ which restricts to $s(f^*t)^ e$ on $X_{f^*t}$. For any $b > 0$ consider the section $s'' = s'(f^*t)^ b$ of $\mathcal{L}^{\otimes n} \otimes f^*\mathcal{M}^{\otimes (e + b)m}$. Then $X_{s''} = (X_{f^*t})_ s$ is an affine open of $X$ containing $x$.
L77: Picking $b$ such that $n$ divides $e + b$ we see $\mathcal{L}^{\otimes n} \otimes f^*\mathcal{M}^{\otimes (e + b)m}$ is the $n$th power of $\mathcal{L} \otimes f^*\mathcal{M}^{\otimes a}$ for some $a$ and we can get any $a$ divisible by $m$ and big enough. Since $X$ is quasi-compact a finite number of these affine opens cover $X$. We conclude that for some $a$ sufficiently divisible and large enough the invertible sheaf $\mathcal{L} \otimes f^*\mathcal{M}^{\otimes a}$ is ample on $X$.
L78: On the other hand, we know that $\mathcal{M}^{\otimes c}$ (and hence its pullback to $X$) is globally generated for all $c \gg 0$ by Properties, Proposition 【18†28.27.13】. Thus $\mathcal{L} \otimes f^*\mathcal{M}^{\otimes a + c}$ is ample (Properties, Lemma 【36†28.27.5】) for $c \gg 0$ and (1) is proved.
L79: Part (2) follows from Lemma 【31†29.38.6】, Properties, Lemma 【14†28.27.2】, and part (1). $\square$
L80: 
L81: 【37†Lemma 29.38.8.】 Let $g : Y \to S$ and $f : X \to Y$ be morphisms of schemes. Let $\mathcal{M}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_ Y$-module. Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_ X$-module. If $S$ is quasi-compact, $\mathcal{M}$ is $g$-ample, and $\mathcal{L}$ is $f$-ample, then $\mathcal{L} \otimes f^*\mathcal{M}^{\otimes a}$ is $g \circ f$-ample for $a \gg 0$.
L82: Proof. Let $S = \bigcup _{i = 1, \ldots , n} V_ i$ be a finite affine open covering. By Lemma 【19†29.38.4】 it suffices to prove that $\mathcal{L} \otimes f^*\mathcal{M}^{\otimes a}$ is ample on $(g \circ f)^{-1}(V_ i)$ for $i = 1, \ldots , n$. Thus the lemma follows from Lemma 【33†29.38.7】. $\square$
L83: 【38†Lemma 29.38.9.】 Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_ X$-module. Let $S' \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $f' : X' \to S'$ be the base change of $f$ and denote $\mathcal{L}'$ the pullback of $\mathcal{L}$ to $X'$. If $\mathcal{L}$ is $f$-ample, then $\mathcal{L}'$ is $f'$-ample.
L84: Proof. By Lemma 【19†29.38.4】 it suffices to find an affine open covering $S' = \bigcup U'_ i$ such that $\mathcal{L}'$ restricts to an ample invertible sheaf on $(f')^{-1}(U_ i')$ for all $i$. We may choose $U'_ i$ mapping into an affine open $U_ i \subset S$. In this case the morphism $(f')^{-1}(U'_ i) \to f^{-1}(U_ i)$ is affine as a base change of the affine morphism $U'_ i \to U_ i$ (Lemma 【39†29.11.9】). Thus $\mathcal{L}'|_{(f')^{-1}(U'_ i)}$ is ample by Lemma 【33†29.38.7】. $\square$
L85: 【40†Lemma 29.38.10.】 Let $g : Y \to S$ and $f : X \to Y$ be morphisms of schemes. Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_ X$-module. If $\mathcal{L}$ is $g \circ f$-ample and $f$ is quasi-compact【41†^{1}】 then $\mathcal{L}$ is $f$-ample.
L86: Proof. Assume $f$ is quasi-compact and $\mathcal{L}$ is $g \circ f$-ample. Let $U \subset S$ be an affine open and let $V \subset Y$ be an affine open with $g(V) \subset U$. Then $\mathcal{L}|_{(g \circ f)^{-1}(U)}$ is ample on $(g \circ f)^{-1}(U)$ by assumption. Since $f^{-1}(V) \subset (g \circ f)^{-1}(U)$ we see that $\mathcal{L}|_{f^{-1}(V)}$ is ample on $f^{-1}(V)$ by Properties, Lemma 【42†28.27.14】.
L87: Namely, $f^{-1}(V) \to (g \circ f)^{-1}(U)$ is a quasi-compact open immersion by Schemes, Lemma 【43†26.21.14】 as $(g \circ f)^{-1}(U)$ is separated (Properties, Lemma 【17†28.27.8】) and $f^{-1}(V)$ is quasi-compact (as $f$ is quasi-compact). Thus we conclude that $\mathcal{L}$ is $f$-ample by Lemma 【19†29.38.4】. $\square$
L88: 【44†[1]】 This follows if $g$ is quasi-separated by Schemes, Lemma 【43†26.21.14】.

L16: ## 29.20 Excellent schemes
L17: 
L18: We recall that a ring is quasi-excellent if it is a G-ring and J-2. A ring is excellent if it is quasi-excellent and universally catenary.
L19: 
L20: 【11†Definition 29.20.1.】 Let $X$ be a scheme.
L21: 
L22:   1. We say $X$ is quasi-excellent if for every $x \in X$ there exists an affine open neighbourhood $x \in U \subset X$ such that the ring $\mathcal{O}_ X(U)$ is quasi-excellent (see More on Algebra, Definition 【12†15.53.1】).
L23:   2. We say $X$ is excellent if for every $x \in X$ there exists an affine open neighbourhood $x \in U \subset X$ such that the ring $\mathcal{O}_ X(U)$ is excellent (see More on Algebra, Definition 【12†15.53.1】).
L24: 
L25: Quasi-excellent schemes are locally Noetherian (G-rings are Noetherian).
L26: 
L27: 【13†Lemma 29.20.2.】 Let $X$ be a scheme. The following are equivalent
L28: 
L29:   1. $X$ is quasi-excellent, and
L30: 
L31:   2. $X$ is a G-scheme and J-2.
L32: Proof. The implication (1) $\Rightarrow $ (2) follows on combining the definition of quasi-excellent schemes (Definition 【11†29.20.1】), the definition of quasi-excellent rings (More on Algebra, Definition 【12†15.53.1】), the definition of G-schemes (Properties, Definition 【14†28.14.1】), and Lemma 【15†29.19.2】. Conversely, if $X$ is a G-scheme and J-2, then for any $x \in X$ we can find an affine open neighbourhood $x \in U \subset X$ such that $\mathcal{O}_ X(U)$ is a G-ring.
L33: By Lemma 【15†29.19.2】 the ring $\mathcal{O}_ X(U)$ is also J-2, whence quasi-excellent. $\square$
L34: 【16†Lemma 29.20.3.】 A quasi-excellent scheme is Nagata.
L35: 
L36: Proof. See More on Algebra, Lemma 【17†15.53.5】. $\square$
L37: 
L38: 【18†Lemma 29.20.4.】 Let $X$ be a scheme. The following are equivalent
L39: 
L40:   1. $X$ is excellent, and
L41: 
L42:   2. $X$ is quasi-excellent and universally catenary.
L43: Proof. Assume (1). Since excellent rings are quasi-excellent, it is clear that $X$ is quasi-excellent. Since excellent rings are universally catenary, it also follows that $X$ is universally catenary by Lemma 【19†29.17.2】. Assume (2). Let $x \in X$. Since $X$ is quasi-excellent there exists an affine open neighbourhood $x \in U \subset X$ such that $\mathcal{O}_ X(U)$ is quasi-excellent.
L44: Since $X$ is universally category, the ring $\mathcal{O}_ X(U)$ is also universally catenary by Lemma 【19†29.17.2】, whence excellent. $\square$
L45: 【20†Lemma 29.20.5.】 Let $X$ be a scheme. The following are equivalent:
L46: 
L47:   1. The scheme $X$ is (quasi-)excellent.
L48: 
L49:   2. For every affine open $U \subset X$ the ring $\mathcal{O}_ X(U)$ is (quasi-)excellent.
L50: 
L51:   3. There exists an affine open covering $X = \bigcup U_ i$ such that each $\mathcal{O}_ X(U_ i)$ is (quasi-)excellent.
L52: 
L53:   4. There exists an open covering $X = \bigcup X_ j$ such that each open subscheme $X_ j$ is (quasi-)excellent.
L54: Moreover, if $X$ is (quasi-)excellent then every open subscheme is (quasi-)excellent.
L55: 
L56: Proof. By Lemma 【13†29.20.2】 being quasi-excellent is the same as being a G-scheme and J-2. Thus for the quasi-excellent case, the lemma follows from Lemma 【15†29.19.2】 and Properties, Lemma 【21†28.14.3】. For the excellent case, use Lemma 【18†29.20.4】, the quasi-excellent case, and Lemma 【19†29.17.2】. $\square$
L57: 【22†Lemma 29.20.6.】 Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism. If $S$ is (quasi-)excellent and $f$ locally of finite type then $X$ is (quasi-)excellent.
L58: 
L59: Proof. See More on Algebra, Lemma 【23†15.53.2】. $\square$
L60: 
L61: 【24†Lemma 29.20.7.】 The following types of schemes are excellent.
L62: 
L63:   1. Any scheme locally of finite type over a field.
L64: 
L65:   2. Any scheme locally of finite type over a Noetherian complete local ring.
L66: 
L67:   3. Any scheme locally of finite type over $\mathbf{Z}$.
L68:   4. Any scheme locally of finite type over a Dedekind ring of characteristic zero.
L69: 
L70: Proof. By Lemmas 【20†29.20.5】 and 【22†29.20.6】 we only need to show that the rings mentioned above are excellent. For this see More on Algebra, Proposition 【25†15.53.3】. $\square$

L22: 【8†Lemma 26.10.4.】 Let $f : Y \to X$ be an immersion of schemes. Then $f$ is a closed immersion if and only if $f(Y) \subset X$ is a closed subset.
L23: Proof. If $f$ is a closed immersion then $f(Y)$ is closed by definition. Conversely, suppose that $f(Y)$ is closed. By definition there exists an open subscheme $U \subset X$ such that $f$ is the composition of a closed immersion $i : Y \to U$ and the open immersion $j : U \to X$. Let $\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}_ U$ be the quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals associated to the closed immersion $i$.
L24: Note that $\mathcal{I}|_{U \setminus i(Y)} = \mathcal{O}_{U \setminus i(Y)} = \mathcal{O}_{X \setminus i(Y)}|_{U \setminus i(Y)}$. Thus we may glue (see Sheaves, Section 【14†6.33】) $\mathcal{I}$ and $\mathcal{O}_{X \setminus i(Y)}$ to a sheaf of ideals $\mathcal{J} \subset \mathcal{O}_ X$. Since every point of $X$ has a neighbourhood where $\mathcal{J}$ is quasi-coherent, we see that $\mathcal{J}$ is quasi-coherent (in particular locally generated by sections).
L25: By construction $\mathcal{O}_ X/\mathcal{J}$ is supported on $U$ and, restricted there, equal to $\mathcal{O}_ U/\mathcal{I}$. Thus we see that the closed subspaces associated to $\mathcal{I}$ and $\mathcal{J}$ are canonically isomorphic, see Example 【15†26.4.3】. In particular the closed subspace of $U$ associated to $\mathcal{I}$ is isomorphic to a closed subspace of $X$.
L26: Since $Y \to U$ is identified with the closed subspace associated to $\mathcal{I}$, see Lemma 【16†26.4.5】, we conclude that $Y \to U \to X$ is a closed immersion. $\square$
